Imputed means and SDs with their standard errors for every study of a data frame

Source: R/se_imputed_df.R
se_imputed_df.Rd

The data-frame interface of se_imputed for a meta-analysis: one row per study, with the columns that such a data set usually carries (the sample size, the minimum, the first quartile, the median, the third quartile, the maximum, and the sample mean and SD where a study gives them). For each row the function reads which values are present, decides the data-reporting scenario, imputes the mean and the SD where they are not given, and appends them with their standard errors: the naive \(\hat\sigma/\sqrt n\) that treats the imputed mean as a sample mean, and the plug-in standard errors \(C_\mu(n)\hat\sigma\) and \(C_\sigma(n)\hat\sigma\) built from the factors of Wu, Shi and Tong (2026).

Usage

se_imputed_df(
  data,
  n = "n",
  min = "min",
  q1 = "q1",
  med = "med",
  q3 = "q3",
  max = "max",
  mean = "mean",
  sd = "sd",
  suffix = "",
  version = c("blue", "wan_luo_shi"),
  prefer = c("sample", "imputed"),
  append = TRUE,
  type = 7
)

Arguments

data

A data frame, one row per study.

n, min, q1, med, q3, max, mean, sd

The names of the columns holding the sample size, the minimum, the first quartile, the median, the third quartile, the maximum, and the sample mean and SD, each with suffix appended. An argument set to NULL, or naming a column that data does not have, counts as absent for every row. A missing value (NA) counts as absent for that row. The columns must be numeric; a column that is all NA may be logical, as read.csv() reads such a column.

suffix

A string appended to every column name above and to every output column, for data sets that carry two groups side by side (".g1", ".g2"). The default is the empty string.

version

"blue" (default) or "wan_luo_shi", as in se_imputed.

prefer

What to use for a row that has both a summary and a sample mean and SD: "sample" (default), the sample statistics, or "imputed".

append

TRUE (default) returns data with the output columns appended; FALSE returns the output columns alone.

type

The definition of the reported sample quantiles, 1 to 9 as in quantile; 7, R's default. One value for every row.

Value

A data frame. The output columns, each with suffix appended, are scenario ("S1", "S2", "S3", "sample" or "mean_range", see Details), mu_hat, sigma_hat, se_naive (\(\hat\sigma/\sqrt n\)), se_mu (\(C_\mu(n)\hat\sigma\) for an imputed mean, \(\hat\sigma/\sqrt n\) for a sample mean), se_sigma (\(C_\sigma(n)\hat\sigma\) for an imputed SD, and for a sample SD \(\mathrm{sd}\sqrt{1 - b_S(n)^2}\), the standard deviation of a sample SD under normality with the SD plugged in), version_used ("blue", "wan_luo_shi", or "sample" when nothing is imputed) and exact (TRUE for a row with an imputed value, whose factors are computed exactly at its \(n\), NA for a "sample" row).

Details

The scenario of a row is read off its non-missing values, in this order. A sample mean and SD give "sample", the two used as they are, unless prefer = "imputed" and the row also has a complete summary. All five values give "S3"; the first quartile, the median and the third quartile give "S2" (a single extreme beside them is ignored); the minimum, the median and the maximum give "S1". A mean with the minimum and the maximum, and no SD, gives "mean_range" when no summary is complete: the mean is kept as the sample mean, and the SD is imputed from the two extremes alone, as the range divided by its expected value in a normal sample of size \(n\) (the BLUE of \(\sigma\) from the extremes, under version = "blue") or by the closed-form divisor \(\xi(n)\) of the Wan-Luo-Shi version (under "wan_luo_shi"), with se_sigma \(= C_\sigma(n)\hat\sigma\) from the exact moments of the two extremes. These are the SD estimators of "S1" for a sample whose median sits at the center of the order statistics, where the median carries no weight, computed here without a median, so the quantile definition type plays no part. Such a row has se_naive and se_mu both equal to \(\hat\sigma/\sqrt n\), the standard error of a sample mean with the imputed SD plugged in, and needs \(n \ge 3\). A mean outside its range gets NA, as an error in the row. A mean without an SD beside a complete summary is ignored, and the summary gives both estimates.

A row with none of these, with a missing, infinite or non-integer sample size, with a non-finite mean, with a non-finite, negative or zero SD, with a summary whose values are all equal or a range of zero (its imputed SD is zero), with values out of order or a mean outside its reported range, gets NA in every output column and is named in one warning with its reason; the function does not stop, so that the whole table comes back. A standard error of zero would give the study an infinite inverse-variance weight, which is why such a row is set to NA rather than kept. Output columns that an earlier call left in data are replaced, so a data frame can be run again after a value, the version or the type changes.

Every imputed row is computed exactly at its own \(n\), as in se_imputed: at a sample size not of the form \(4Q + 1\) the reported quartiles are interpolated under definition type.

Assumptions: independent normal data within each study. The standard errors are plug-in quantities, \(\sigma\) replaced by \(\hat\sigma\); their reference distribution is not Student's t and is not supplied by this version. A study whose data are visibly skewed (the quartiles far from symmetric around the median) should be screened before the normal-model estimators are applied, as the source papers of those estimators recommend.

References

Wu Z, Shi J, Tong T (2026). Precision of the imputed mean and standard deviation from a five-number summary. Manuscript.

See also

se_imputed for one study, se_imputed_diff for two groups per row, pool_imputed to pool the studies.

Examples

studies <- data.frame(n = c(25, 30, 41, 25, 35),
                      min = c(3, NA, 1, NA, 2), q1 = c(10, 10, 9, NA, NA),
                      med = c(12, 12, 12, NA, NA), q3 = c(15, 15, 16, NA, NA),
                      max = c(30, NA, 30, NA, 28),
                      mean = c(NA, NA, NA, 13, 12), sd = c(NA, NA, NA, 3, NA))
se_imputed_df(studies)   # S3, S2, S1, a sample mean and SD, a mean with the range
#>    n min q1 med q3 max mean sd   scenario   mu_hat sigma_hat  se_naive
#> 1 25   3 10  12 15  30   NA NA         S3 13.02497  5.907023 1.1814046
#> 2 30  NA 10  12 15  NA   NA NA         S2 12.35952  3.883653 0.7090548
#> 3 41   1  9  12 16  30   NA NA         S3 12.72772  6.168222 0.9633144
#> 4 25  NA NA  NA NA  NA   13  3     sample 13.00000  3.000000 0.6000000
#> 5 35   2 NA  NA NA  28   12 NA mean_range 12.00000  6.171054 1.0430985
#>       se_mu  se_sigma version_used exact
#> 1 1.2219709 0.9367854         blue  TRUE
#> 2 0.7573922 0.8191412         blue  TRUE
#> 3 1.0053976 0.7902086         blue  TRUE
#> 4 0.6000000 0.4307056       sample    NA
#> 5 1.0430985 0.9957990         blue  TRUE
se_imputed_df(studies, version = "wan_luo_shi", append = FALSE)
#>     scenario   mu_hat sigma_hat  se_naive     se_mu  se_sigma version_used
#> 1         S3 13.02860  5.914788 1.1829577 1.2235941 0.9387881  wan_luo_shi
#> 2         S2 12.35650  3.892101 0.7105972 0.7590482 0.8227088  wan_luo_shi
#> 3         S3 12.72172  6.175581 0.9644636 1.0066064 0.7924849  wan_luo_shi
#> 4     sample 13.00000  3.000000 0.6000000 0.6000000 0.4307056       sample
#> 5 mean_range 12.00000  6.181485 1.0448616 1.0448616 0.9991682  wan_luo_shi
#>   exact
#> 1  TRUE
#> 2  TRUE
#> 3  TRUE
#> 4    NA
#> 5  TRUE
# columns named as a spreadsheet often names them
names(studies) <- c("N", "Min", "Q1", "Median", "Q3", "Max", "Mean", "SD")
se_imputed_df(studies, n = "N", min = "Min", q1 = "Q1", med = "Median", q3 = "Q3",
              max = "Max", mean = "Mean", sd = "SD", append = FALSE)
#>     scenario   mu_hat sigma_hat  se_naive     se_mu  se_sigma version_used
#> 1         S3 13.02497  5.907023 1.1814046 1.2219709 0.9367854         blue
#> 2         S2 12.35952  3.883653 0.7090548 0.7573922 0.8191412         blue
#> 3         S3 12.72772  6.168222 0.9633144 1.0053976 0.7902086         blue
#> 4     sample 13.00000  3.000000 0.6000000 0.6000000 0.4307056       sample
#> 5 mean_range 12.00000  6.171054 1.0430985 1.0430985 0.9957990         blue
#>   exact
#> 1  TRUE
#> 2  TRUE
#> 3  TRUE
#> 4    NA
#> 5  TRUE
